# Grammarly Pricing in 2026: Is It Worth Paying For?

Grammarly sells several plans, and the right one depends on how much you use it. Below is the current lineup, what you get at each tier, and who should (or shouldn't) upgrade. *Prices are approximate and change often — confirm on the official site before buying.*

## Grammarly Plans at a Glance

| Plan | Price | What You Get |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Free | $0 | grammar, spelling, punctuation |
| Premium | ~$12/mo | tone, clarity, plagiarism |
| Business | ~$15/seat/mo | team style guide |

## Which Plan Should You Pick?

- **Free / trial:** best for testing the waters. anyone who writes in English can try it without risk.

- **Mid tier (~$12/mo):** the sweet spot for most individuals who use Grammarly regularly.

- **Top tier (~$15/seat/mo):** for power users and teams that need the extra limits or seats.


## Is Grammarly Worth Paying For?

If the writing-quality assistant is central to your work — anyone who writes in English — the paid plan pays for itself quickly. If you only need occasional help, the free tier or a cheaper alternative may be enough.

**See the current offer:** {{AFFILIATE_GRAMMARLY}}

## Cheaper Alternatives

If the price is the blocker, these alternatives cost less or include a free plan:

- [[link:/tools/24|QuillBot]] — the paraphrasing & summarizer
- [[link:/tools/74|Copy.ai]] — the go-to sales & marketing copy tool
- [[link:/tools/23|Rytr]] — the budget-friendly AI writer

## Frequently Asked Questions

### How much does Grammarly cost?

Grammarly starts at $0 and goes up to ~$15/seat/mo on the top tier. Exact pricing changes, so check the official site.

### Does Grammarly have a free plan?

Yes — the free tier covers basic use.

### Is Grammarly worth the money?

For its core audience (anyone who writes in English), yes. Lighter users may be fine on a free or cheaper alternative.
